title: Distributions Without Lies
objective: After this lesson you will be able to show spread honestly (bin-stability notes, box plots, skew language), choose bins deliberately, and reject single-number summaries where shape matters.
why: Averages hide bimodality, coarse bins merge peaks, and 'normal-ish' assumptions break on skew: two customer groups (budget + premium) average into a middle that exists nowhere. Distribution views reveal what summaries conceal — and bin choices determine what's visible, making bins a methodological decision with notes, not defaults.

blocks.text: Bin count/width decides visible shape: 3 bins merge modes into uniformity; 50 bins noise every wiggle into false peaks. Practice: try 5/10/20 bins, keep conclusions stable across all three, report the chosen bins with the stability note. Single-binning conclusions are binning artifacts until proven otherwise.

blocks.caption: Bin-count sweep: stable shapes earn conclusions

blocks.text: Box plots: five numbers, zero hiding

Box plots compress distributions honestly: median (typical), quartiles (middle-50 spread), whiskers (1.5×IQR range), points beyond (outliers named individually). Pair with sample sizes — identical boxes from n=8 vs n=8000 mean different things. Skew reads directly (median off-center, long whisker side). No bin decisions required: boxes dodge the binning problem entirely.

blocks.title: Means need company
blocks.text: A mean without spread and n is a rumor with decimals: pair every reported mean with its distribution shape (or at minimum SD + n). Decision-makers acting on lone means inherit hidden skew.

blocks.title: Stabilize the shape
blocks.note: Run it: 5 bins show two peaks (4,0,0,0,4 shape); 2 bins merge everything (4,4 — uniformity lie). Stability across counts separates shapes from artifacts.

items: Sweep bin counts (5/10/20): stable shapes conclude, shifting shapes suspect artifacts
Box plots compress honestly (median/quartiles/whiskers/outliers) + always with n
Skew language precise (direction + whisker side); single means never substitute for shapes

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice histograms and map both shapes. (b) Add a uniform dataset (1..8) at 5 bins and contrast its shape with bimodal's. (c) State the bin-stability note you would publish alongside the bimodal chart.
hints: Bimodal 5-bin: two peaks separated; 2-bin: merged uniformity (the lie demonstrated).
Uniform 1..8 at 5 bins: roughly even counts — compare against bimodal's clustered shape (same bins, different truth).
Note names bins tried (5/10/20), stability verdict (peaks persist), and n (8 points — small-sample caveat attached).
exercise.why: Artifact demonstration (merged uniformity), contrast control (uniform at same bins), and published bin notes (method transparency) are the three distribution judgments.
exercise.code: // Bin-sweep pattern: multiple counts, stability verdict, published note.

options: No: sweep 5/10/20 first — coarse bins merge modes into false uniformity; stability earns conclusions
quiz.explain: Bin width chooses visible shape: uniformity at one count is a candidate artifact until multi-count stability proves otherwise.

quiz.q: Mean revenue reported alone, n=12, skewed. Missing?
options: Distribution + n: skew pulls means from typicals; box/histogram plus sample size, never lone means on skew
quiz.explain: Single summaries conceal spread and skew; small n amplifies the lie. Shapes plus counts, always.

quiz.q: Box plot without n, two groups compared. Gap?
options: Sample sizes: identical boxes at n=8 vs n=8000 mean different things (noise vs truth)
quiz.explain: Boxes compress; n contextualizes. Comparisons need both shape and evidence weight.

summary: Sweep bins, note stability, box with n, language skew precisely. Shapes earn conclusions; single numbers don't.
